docs.title: Govern GitHub repositories as declared state
Repository governance you can review before it changes anything
docs.text:
Octoform compares a YAML policy with the current state of your GitHub repositories, reports the exact drift, and applies only the changes you approve.

Get started View the source

docs.title: Declarative by default
docs.text: Omitted settings stay unmanaged. Explicit values participate in a deterministic plan, so a small configuration does not acquire accidental side effects.

docs.title: Capability-driven
docs.text: GitHub's response, the owner, repository visibility, and current token determine whether a change is available. Product-plan names are diagnostic context, not authorization logic.

docs.title: Safe automation
docs.text: audit and plan are read-only. apply presents the same planned changes and requires confirmation unless an operator deliberately enables non-interactive execution.

docs.title: A minimal policy
docs.text:
octoform.yml
owner: your-account

defaults:
  features:
    wiki: false
  security:
    vulnerability_alerts: true

octoform plan

The current documentation describes Octoform 0.3.1. Use the version selector after publication to keep procedures aligned with the release you operate.

docs.title: Architecture overview
docs.text:
Octoform separates declaration, observation, planning, and mutation. The planner is deterministic: the same normalized desired and observed state produces the same ordered changes.

flowchart LR
    Operator[Operator or CI] --> Config[octoform.yml]
    Config --> Resolve[Resolve effective policy]
    GitHub[GitHub API] --> Observe[Observe current state]
    Resolve --> Plan[Build deterministic plan]
    Observe --> Plan
    Plan --> Report[Report drift and blocked changes]
    Report --> Confirm{Apply approved?}
    Confirm -->|No| Stop[No mutation]
    Confirm -->|Yes| Apply[Apply ordered changes]
    Apply --> GitHub

docs.title: Core safety properties
docs.text:
1. Omission means unmanaged, not disabled or deleted.
  2. Unreadable state blocks a change instead of producing a guessed diff.
  3. Capability decisions use API evidence rather than hard-coded product plans.
  4. apply operates on the plan already shown to the operator.
  5. Destructive absence-based reconciliation is outside the normal contract.

The application repository contains the current domain model and implementation tests for these properties.

docs.title: Contribute to the documentation
docs.text: Documentation changes use the same review standard as application changes. A procedure must be accurate for the version it names, safe to follow, and useful without requiring the reader to inspect Octoform's implementation.

docs.title: Before opening a pull request
docs.text:
1. Check whether the change describes released behavior.
  2. State prerequisites, permissions, applicability, result, and recovery.
  3. Use fictitious owners, repositories, tokens, and file paths.
  4. Run the complete local verification command.
  5. Inspect the generated site in both light and dark modes at mobile and desktop widths.

See the repository contribution guide for environment setup, commands, and the review checklist.

docs.title: Get started
docs.text: This path installs Octoform, authenticates it for the repositories you intend to inspect, and produces a read-only plan. No repository is changed.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Node.js 20 or newer
  • a GitHub token that can read the target repositories
  • a personal account or organization login to use as owner

Prefer a fine-grained personal access token or GitHub App installation token with access limited to the repositories and permissions required by your policy.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
npm install --global @hector21/octoform
octoform --help

docs.title: Authenticate
docs.text:
macOS and LinuxPowerShell 
export GITHUB_TOKEN="your-token"

$env:GITHUB_TOKEN = "your-token"

Do not write the token into octoform.yml, shell history, examples, logs, or a committed workflow. In GitHub Actions, provide it through the workflow's permission-scoped token or an approved secret source.

docs.title: Create the policy
docs.text:
octoform.yml
owner: your-account

defaults:
  features:
    wiki: false

An omitted key is unmanaged. The example asks Octoform to disable wikis and makes no claim about any other repository setting.

docs.title: Review a plan
docs.text:
octoform plan --config octoform.yml

Read blocked and unsupported results as evidence, not skipped work. Octoform does not guess that an unreadable setting is safe to overwrite.

Keep the first run read-only

Confirm owner selection, repository scope, token permissions, and planned values before using octoform apply.

docs.title: Security and trust
docs.text: Octoform operates with the authority of the token provided to it. A safe setup starts with the smallest useful repository selection and permission set, then expands only when a declared capability requires it.

docs.title: Trust boundaries
docs.text: Boundary Contract Configuration Contains desired state and local file paths, never token values Token input Read from GITHUB_TOKEN, then GH_TOKEN; never written to the plan audit and plan Read-only GitHub operations apply Uses the reviewed plan, asks for confirmation, and reports each result Unreadable state Reported as blocked instead of assumed absent or disabled Unsupported capability Reported with evidence from the owner, repository, token, and endpoint

docs.title: Token handling
docs.text:
• Use a short-lived GitHub App token for automation when practical.
  • Restrict fine-grained tokens to the repositories under governance.
  • Grant write permissions only for capabilities present in the policy.
  • Mask secrets in CI and never enable shell tracing around authentication.
  • Revoke or rotate a token immediately if it appears in output or history.

Octoform 0.3.1 performs no GraphQL request. Its current REST permissions vary by feature: repository administration, contents, environments, rules, security events, and organization custom properties are distinct capabilities.

docs.title: Reporting a vulnerability
docs.text: Do not open a public issue for a suspected vulnerability or exposed credential. Follow the private reporting instructions in the security policy.
